question: A grocer sells sugar at a 10% loss. Had he sold it for ₹0.60 more per kg, he would have gained 8%. What is the cost price of sugar per kg?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change = 8% − (−10%) = 18%

This 18% gap corresponds to ₹0.60 price difference.

18% of CP = 0.60

CP = (0.60 ÷ 18) × 100 = 60 ÷ 18

CP = 3.33

**∴ Answer = ₹3.33**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial loss = 10%, Potential gain = 8%, Increase in price = ₹0.60 per kg
